goal:
In kestrel-team (Python; gate `uv run --locked python -m pytest tests/ -q`,
fully mocked, no network; base = main 626c87f), make the engine refuse a
gate it cannot run: an `audit.gate` that `shlex.split` turns into tokens a
shell would read as operators. READ CLAUDE.md FIRST. Nothing else changes.
Open no PR; the PR and the merge are the operator's.

Facts (seat, 2026-11-01, on 626c87f). `core/cloud_audit.py` line 422
`code, out = run.run(check, shlex.split(gate), work)` inside `_run_gate`
(421–423): the gate runs with no shell (`_Runner.run`, 161–180, `shell=False`
for the gate; only the mutation gets a shell). `docs/cloud.md` 263–265 says
so ("split with `shlex` (no shell)"). Nothing checks the tokens: `core/cloud.py`
`check_cloud_eligible` (223–240) refuses on mode, status and route only, and
`prepare` (448–) calls it at 465, pushes the task branch at 481
(`deliver_task`) and copies the declaration into `prepared.json` at 502
(`"audit": item.audit.to_dict() if item.audit else None`) with no look at
`gate`. On 2026-11-01 artemis-helm queue/0002 declared `gate: npm ci
--no-audit --no-fund && npm test`; `shlex.split` of that is `['npm', 'ci',
'--no-audit', '--no-fund', '&&', 'npm', 'test']`, so the audit ran `npm ci
'&&' npm test`, `npm test` never ran, `host_gate PASS … exited 0: added 84
packages in 618ms` on the installer alone, and `mutation FAIL the gate
stayed green`. `spawner cloud prepare` had accepted the string without a
word. A gate is a claim only when it is the command the operator meant.

Do this. (1) `core/cloud.py`: add `import shlex` between `import os` (43)
and `import subprocess` (44). After `ENVIRONMENT_ENV` (70) add two
module-level constants and one function, exactly:
    SHELL_OPERATORS = ("&&", "||", ";", "|", ">", ">>", "<", "2>&1")
    GATE_NOT_ONE_ARGV = (
        "audit.gate carries the shell operator {token!r}: the audit runs the gate with "
        "no shell (shlex.split), so `{gate}` would hand it to the command as a plain "
        "argument. Declare the gate as one argv, e.g. bash -c \"npm ci && npm test\"."
    )
    def gate_shell_operator(gate: str) -> Optional[str]:
        return next((t for t in shlex.split(gate) if t in SHELL_OPERATORS), None)
with a `#:` comment on `SHELL_OPERATORS` naming artemis-helm queue/0002 as
the case, and a docstring on the function ("a gate the audit can run is one
argv"). (2) Call site one, in `check_cloud_eligible`, after the route check
(the `raise` that ends at 240), exactly these three lines, as code:
    token = gate_shell_operator(item.audit.gate) if item.audit else None
    if token is not None:
        raise CloudPrepareError(GATE_NOT_ONE_ARGV.format(token=token, gate=item.audit.gate))
The last two lines are exactly `    if token is not None:` then
`        raise CloudPrepareError(GATE_NOT_ONE_ARGV.format(token=token, gate=item.audit.gate))`:
the declared mutation removes them by exact text. This sits in the function
`prepare` calls at 465, before `deliver_task` at 481: the refusal is decided
before the remote is touched (module doc 34–36), and `--dry-run` refuses the
same way. Update the docstring (224–225) to say "whose gate, if any, is one
argv". The CLI already prints `Cloud prepare refused: {e}` and exits 1
(`cli/app.py` 1152–1155), so the refusal line reads exactly
`Cloud prepare refused: audit.gate carries the shell operator '&&': the audit
runs the gate with no shell (shlex.split), so `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund &&
npm test` would hand it to the command as a plain argument. Declare the gate
as one argv, e.g. bash -c "npm ci && npm test".` (3) Call site two, in
`core/cloud_audit.py` `audit()` (577–): after the `declared_by` block ends
at 610 (`declared_by = None`) and before `target = prepared["target_repo"]`
at 612, exactly:
    token = cloud.gate_shell_operator(gate) if gate is not None else None
    if token is not None:
        raise CloudAuditError(cloud.GATE_NOT_ONE_ARGV.format(token=token, gate=gate))
